subject: Hospitality
title: Biophilic Design in Hotels
description: A quick, practical guide to Biophilic Design in Hotels.

hook.text: Biophilic design brings nature indoors—living walls, indoor trees, natural light, water features.

buildup.text: The concept draws from biologist E.O. Wilson's theory: humans have an innate need to connect with nature, even inside buildings.

discovery.text: Hotels with biophilic elements report 15% higher guest satisfaction scores. Nature in design isn't decoration—it's therapeutic.

twist.text: Maintaining living walls and indoor plants is costly and complex. Dead plants signal neglect more than no plants at all.

climax.text: Singapore's PARKROYAL Collection Pickering has 15,000 sqm of sky gardens—more greenery than its floor area.

punchline.text: Living walls, sky gardens, indoor forests. Biophilic design heals guests through nature.

quiz.question: What is biophilic design based on?
options: The theory that humans have an innate need to connect with nature
